Kyoto woodblock print studio born from Takenaka Mokuhan, a hand woodblock printing craftsman studio established 1891; carvers and printers make woodblock prints; also restores old prints and blocks
Asakusa (Tokyo) woodblock print workshop and shop opened 2014 by printer Dave Bull; sells woodblock prints, known for the Ukiyo-e Heroes series

Kyoto collotype atelier making collotypes since 1905; 'the only fine-art printing studio producing color collotypes internationally'; sells limited-edition collotype portfolios via benrido-store.com (museum blog used for standing only; product page https://benrido-store.com/ names it as maker/seller)

add_brands.n: Taohuawu Woodcut New Year Pictures Society
add_brands.says: Suzhou municipal page: the society keeps the Ming multi-block colour overprinting of Taohuawu New Year prints; administration moved to Suzhou Art & Design Technology Institute in 2002
China Daily: its Yangliuqing woodblock print workshop (publicly owned since 1958) crafts 'one of the most renowned Chinese New Year picture brands'
Yangjiabu (Weifang) New Year print shop of inheritor Yang Zhibin; Yangjiabu prints are national intangible heritage and one of China's three major woodblock New Year print schools

SCMP: weekly Jingdezhen market of independent ceramists founded by ceramic artist Caroline Cheng, who established the Pottery Workshop 28 years earlier; PWS (founded 1985) runs studios in Jingdezhen and Shanghai (pws-hub.com)
Cooperative founded 2009 of 27+ Jacmel artisan workshops sharing a quality-controlled shop for paintings and papier-mache; Jacmel described as Haiti's cultural capital famed for papier-mache
Jacmel women artisans' cooperative with a common boutique; with G27 'some of the most professional and talented of Jacmel's artisans'
Fair-trade network (Fairwinds Trading + HAND/EYE Fund) with depots in Jacmel, Port-au-Prince and Croix-des-Bouquets selling signed papier-mache and Croix-des-Bouquets metal art
Gallery specialising in original Haitian paintings and Croix-des-Bouquets metal sculpture (self-description; listed tier)

Gallery and shop of the Craft Potters Association (founded 1958), Bloomsbury opposite the British Museum since 2010; sells studio ceramics by selected CPA members; CPA a member of the International Academy of Ceramics
Studio and gallery founded 1976 by Peter Layton, 'one of the founding fathers of studio glass in the UK'; sells studio glass by Layton and resident artists (self-description)

add_brands.n: Nike Art Foundation (Nike Centre for Art and Culture)
add_brands.says: Lekki (Lagos) gallery of some 8,000 works over five storeys, 'said to be the largest gallery in West Africa'; founded by Nike Davies-Okundaye, with art centres and workshops in Oshogbo, Abuja, Ogidi-Ijumu (nikeartfoundation.com)

KwaZulu-Natal ceramic art studio founded 1985 by Fée Halsted; 80+ Zulu and Zimbabwean artists; collaborations with Hermès and Cole & Son, recognised as a modern collectible at Christie's; founder awarded the Order of Ikhamanga (WMODA museum page used for standing only)

add_brands.n: Uqqurmiut Arts & Crafts (Pangnirtung Print Shop and Tapestry Studio)
add_brands.says: 'Internationally-known Inuit art facility' in Pangnirtung: print shop, tapestry studio and gallery producing limited-edition prints and tapestries sold through galleries across North America; annual Pangnirtung Print Collection since 1973
Baker Lake (Kivalliq) Inuit arts centre named on the Nunavut Development Corporation subsidiaries page (existence only)

add_brands.n: New Zealand Māori Arts and Crafts Institute (Te Puia)
add_brands.says: Aotearoa's leading centre for traditional Māori carving and weaving (statutory since 1963, iwi-owned since 2020); taonga by its students and masters sold through Āhua Gallery
Russia's oldest lacquer miniature centre (Korobov/Lukutin works, Fedoskino artel from 1910); works 'very valuable collectible items' (seller page; facts historical, praise not independent)
